page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-16 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance powered by Ampere Altra processors running at a constant frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance provisions 2 physical cores, translating to 2 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core, thereby eliminating noisy-neighbor issues common to simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an elevated memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per physical core.

Storage and networking resources reflect a network-attached configuration. The VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-16 does not contain local storage devices, requiring users to rely on external cloud storage volumes for all filesystem and persistence needs. There are no discrete GPU accelerators assigned to the instance. Network provisioning includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address for ingress and egress routing.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM balance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding significant memory capacity relative to compute footprint. Arm Neoverse N1 architecture offers reliable core execution efficiency, though workloads must be compiled specifically for the arm64 instruction set architecture. Given its memory profile and dedicated core allocation, the instance is well matched for memory-resident microservices, lightweight database engines, caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, and Arm64 software continuous integration pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-16 is a flexible virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Ampere Altra 3.0 GHz arm64 processor. With 16.0 GB of RAM allocated, the server yields an 8.0 GB per core allocation, providing substantial headroom for memory-dependent tasks without incurring the costs of unneeded processing threads. The instance contains no onboard local storage, depending entirely on remote block storage for persistent data, and does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs. An integrated complimentary public IPv4 address provides direct network accessibility. The single-threaded physical core design ensures consistent performance without hardware thread contention. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-16 is suitable for lightweight databases, in-memory caches, development environments, and containerized web services running on Arm architectures.
